en: The Section on the Dyads beginning with "With Cause and Having Cause," the Wholesome Triplet.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless and is not wholesome, there arises a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless and is not wholesome, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless and is not wholesome, there arises a state that is rootless but not a root-cause and is not wholesome, by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless...

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor a root and is not unwholesome, and also not a root and not unwholesome, there arise states that are neither wholesome nor a root and are not unwholesome, and also not a root and not unwholesome, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither unwholesome nor a root and is not unwholesome, there arises a state that is neither unwholesome nor a root and is not unwholesome, by way of root condition. … three.

Dependent on a state that is neither a cause nor rootless, neither wholesome nor rootless, and neither a cause nor associated with a cause, and is not wholesome, there arises a state that is neither a cause nor rootless and not wholesome by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). ... [Three] (Abbreviated).
In the case of roots, nine ... up to ... in the case of non-disappearance, nine.

Dependent on a state that is neither a cause nor rootless and not unwholesome, there arises a state that is neither a cause nor rootless and not unwholesome by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated).
In the case of root-condition (*hetu*), nine [answers] … pe … in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*), nine.
Dependent on a state that is neither root nor rootless nor indeterminate, there arises a state that is neither root nor rootless nor indeterminate by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
In the case of root, nine … pe … in the case of non-disappearance, nine. (There is no resultant.)
(The "Cause and Cause-Associated" dyad is similar to the "Cause and With-Cause" dyad.)
